## Adversarial Claim Verifier (voter 3/3)

Be SKEPTICAL. Try to REFUTE this claim. ≥2/3 refutations kill it.

## Research question
What are all the major enumerable lists in the Quran — things that have a finite, complete set of items mentioned across the Quran? For example: the 25 prophets mentioned by name, the categories of people (mu'minoon, kafireen etc.), the prohibited things (haram), the signs of Qiyamah, the names/attributes of Allah (Asma ul Husna), angels mentioned by name, animals mentioned, stories/parables, punishments (hudood), pillars of Islam mentioned, rivers of paradise, levels of hell (Jahannam), days/events of the afterlife sequence, battles mentioned, etc. I want a comprehensive meta-list of every topic in the Quran that has a finite enumerable set of items that a researcher would want to list completely.

## Claim under review
"The major signs include specific named figures and events: the Dajjal, the Mahdi, the return of Isa (Jesus), the Sufyani, and Yajuj and Majuj (Gog and Magog), as well as large-scale battles and natural disasters."

**Source:** https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Signs_of_Qiyamah (secondary)
**Supporting quote:** "Major figures: Dajjal, Mahdi, Jesus (Isa), Sufyani, Yajuj and Majuj (Gog and Magog) ... widespread moral failings, great battles ... natural disasters, rampaging evil forces"

## Checklist
1. Is the claim actually supported by the quote, or is it an overreach/misread?
2. WebSearch for contradicting evidence — does any credible source dispute or heavily qualify this?
3. Is the source quality sufficient for the claim's strength? (extraordinary claims need primary sources)
4. Is the claim outdated? (check dates — old claims about fast-moving fields are suspect)
5. Is this a marketing claim / press release / cherry-picked benchmark / forum speculation?

**refuted=true** if: unsupported by quote / contradicted / low-quality source for strong claim / outdated / marketing fluff.
**refuted=false** ONLY if: claim is well-supported, current, and source quality matches claim strength.
Default to refuted=true if uncertain.

Structured output only. Evidence MUST be specific.

Based on the search results, here's comprehensive information about the signs of Qiyamah (Day of Judgment) from Islamic sources:

## Major Signs of Qiyamah

The major signs of Qiyamah include the emergence of Imam Mahdi, the emergence of Dajjal, 'Isa ('alayhis salam) returning to the world, the emergence of Yajuj and Majuj (Gog And Magog), and the sun rising from the west.

### Imam Mahdi

Imam al-Mahdi will be a righteous man from among the descendants of the Prophet Muhammad (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), who will appear at the end of time, through whom Allah will set mankind's affairs straight, and will fill the earth with fairness and justice just as it was filled with wrongdoing and oppression. The name of Imam al-Mahdi will be the same as the name of the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), and his father's name will be the same as that of the father of the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him).

### Dajjal (The Antichrist)

Dajjal is a one-eyed deceiver who will claim to be divine. Maseeh Dajjal will be short, and his legs will be crooked. The hair on his head will be extremely twisted. He will have one eye (with which he can see, and this is the protruding eye about which other ahadeeth inform us), while his other eye will be totally flat.

### Prophet Isa (Jesus)

Prophet Isa will return to defeat Dajjal and rule with peace. He will descend from the heavens to the white minaret in the east of Damascus wearing two garments slightly dyed with Saffron and his hands will be placed on the wings of two angels.

### Yajuj and Majuj (Gog and Magog)

Yajooj and Majooj are barbaric tribes who will spread corruption on Earth. A short period after Prophet Jesus has killed the Dajjal, the two mighty tribes of Yajuj and Ma'juj will appear, causing murder, pillage and devastation wherever they go.

## Order of Events

Isa (peace be upon him) will follow the Mahdi in prayer, which indicates that the Mahdi will appear before Isa, and Isa will kill the Dajjal, which indicates that the Dajjal will appear during the time of the Mahdi.

## Quranic and Hadith Sources

These signs are referenced in authentic hadith collections including Sahih Bukhari, Sahih Muslim, Sunan Abu Dawood, and other authenticated hadith sources. The signs emphasize the temporary nature of this world and call believers to strengthen their faith and righteousness.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about the Sufyani in relation to the Quran, hadith, and signs of the Day of Judgment:

## Overview of the Sufyani

The Sufyani is a figure in Islamic eschatology who is usually portrayed in hadiths as a tyrant who will spread corruption and mischief. Reports about Sufyani are available in both Sunni and Shia Hadith.

## Connection to the Quran

The coming of al-Mahdī and al-Masīḥ ad-Dajjāl and the second coming of ʿĪsā are mentioned in the hadith literature but not the Quran; reports about Sufyani are available in both Sunni and Shia Hadith. In other words, while the Sufyani appears in hadith sources, it is not mentioned directly in the Quran.

## Descriptions in Hadith

It is said that he will kill children and rip out the bellies of women, murder those from the household of the Prophet and rule over Syria. It is also said that when the Mahdi appears, the Sufyani will send an army to seize and kill him, but, when the Sufyani and his army reach the desert of Bayda, they would be swallowed up.

## Authenticity Concerns

Some sources, mostly Sunni, claim that the hadith describing the Sufyani are unreliable and are based on a "garbled version" of a legend "fabricated by traditionists with Shia and pro-'Abbasid sentiments". At least one source considers the hadith of Sufyani unsound by quoting Al-Albani as declaring it munkar (going against another sahih, or sound, hadith and reported to have a weak narrator) and citing imperfections in the isnad (chain of transmitters).

input.evidence: The claim has two significant problems. First, the Sufyani is a contested figure: Sunni hadith scholars including Al-Albani have declared Sufyani hadiths munkar (weak/rejected), and some sources describe them as fabricated by traditionists with Shia and pro-Abbasid sentiments. Listing the Sufyani alongside Dajjal, Mahdi, Isa, and Yajuj wa Majuj as a co-equal "major sign" overstates disputed material. Second, and more fundamentally, the Mahdi and Dajjal are not mentioned in the Quran at all — they appear only in hadith literature. The Quran does mention Yajuj and Majuj (18:94, 21:96) and Isa, but the full list of named figures in the claim derives from hadith, not Quranic text. The research question is specifically about "things mentioned across the Quran," making this claim a category error: it conflates Quranic content with hadith eschatology. The Wikipedia secondary source is insufficient to validate a claim about Quranic enumeration, and the Sufyani's inclusion is actively disputed by mainstream Sunni scholarship.
